title: One approval, then unattended: light the existing auto-approval engine so Gate 2 and Gate 3 close on machine evidence by default
description:
Filed 2026-09-09 by architect-ed42e60a on the OWNER'S DIRECTION of the same day: "we dont want moe-next to be stuck all the time for user approval we can approve the plan at the start but thats it". An external review the same day recommended MORE human gates (preview approval required before release); the owner wants ONE — at plan/contract time — and the rest unattended, with a human ABLE to intervene but not REQUIRED.

THE ENGINE ALREADY EXISTS AND IS DARK — do not let a planner build a new approval-policy subsystem. Measured 2026-09-04 (Serena memory design-710-auto-approval-exists-but-dark), re-confirm at HEAD before planning:
- packages/core/src/policy/policy-evaluation.ts:157 `if (fold.optIns.some((entry) => entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)))` is the decision.
- policy-contract.ts:24 POLICY_RISK_TIERS = ["R0","R1","R2","R3"]; :28 POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS = ["R0","R1"] — only R0/R1 may ever be automatic; R2/R3 are human-only; manual is the default; :51 no tier-bearing fact leaves computedTier null (never a silent R0). Fail-safe is the right way round.
- Also present: policy-validation.ts:181,215-217, policy-slice-digest.ts:51,54, policy-composition.ts:140-166, apps/daemon/src/http/policy-read.ts:40,45, ops-screens.tsx:157.
- DARK FOR TWO SEAMS: (1) every production caller passes `autoApprovalOptIns: []` (apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100); only fixtures carry values. (2) apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/goal-model.ts:90 `AdvisoryRiskClass = "STANDARD"|"ELEVATED"|"RESTRICTED"` is set at new-goal-form.tsx:99 and consumed ONLY by live-goal-create.ts:50 as a line of prose. No mapping to R0..R3 exists.
- GREP TRAP: `requiresApproval|needsApproval|shouldAutoApprove` returns ZERO — the decision is spelled `fold.optIns.some(...)`. Absence of those names is not absence of the feature.

WHAT THIS ROW DOES: at the one human approval (plan/contract, Gate 1), the operator's choice becomes durable auto-approval opt-ins for preview.decide and release.decide at the tiers the policy engine permits; the risk class chosen on the goal form maps to a policy tier instead of becoming prose; the gates then close on machine evidence — the preview receipt for Gate 2, the release dossier with zero gaps for Gate 3 — with no operator keystroke. A human can still decide either gate manually, and a manual REJECT wins. R2/R3 stay human-only by the engine's own rule; this row does not widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS.

PREREQUISITE, declared in dependsOn: task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada (release dossier bound to criterion receipts at the released SHA). Auto-releasing on today's dossier would auto-release on evidence weaker than goal closure demands — the exact defect the review found. Also note task-9dbe28fdccc546dfbbbf9b32f68e7c61 (accepted node lands nothing -> checkout BLOCKED forever) is the other thing that kills an unattended run; it is an independent seam and filed separately in epic-8ebe6417.

WHO SUBMITS THE AUTOMATIC DECISION: preview.decide and release.decide are OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS (daemon-command-vocabulary.ts:378,405), human-only and MCP-excluded by deliberate rulings (comment-18dc557c, epic rail on Gate kinds). The planner must decide the principal that carries an automatic decision — the operator principal acting under a recorded opt-in is the narrowest shape already in the tree (precedent: the typed SOFT_POLICY_WAIVER arm at daemon-command-registry.ts:315-328) — and must NOT widen the MCP allowlist or let an agent seat decide a gate. The decision record must name the opt-in it acted under so a reviewer can tell an automatic approval from a human one. A malformed copy of this row (task-d4eb03f1, empty description) was deleted minutes before this one was filed.
definitionOfDone: A goal created with an R0/R1-mapped risk class and an approved plan reaches a DEPLOYED preview and then a released PR with ZERO further human decisions, proven by a journey arm that asserts each gate's decision record names the durable opt-in it acted under (not merely that the outcome was ACCEPTED).
A goal mapped to R2 or R3 is NOT auto-approved at either gate: the arm asserts the gate stays pending for a human and that POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is unchanged at ["R0","R1"].
A human REJECT on a gate wins over an opt-in: an arm records a manual REJECT then proves the automatic path does not overturn it, asserting the refusal code.

The goal form's risk class maps to a policy tier through one typed mapping (no prose line), with an arm asserting every AdvisoryRiskClass value maps to exactly one POLICY_RISK_TIER and every tier is reachable — set equality both directions.

Production composition no longer passes autoApprovalOptIns: [] unconditionally — an arm on the live dispatch payload asserts the opt-ins recorded at Gate 1 are carried; and no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision: the MCP allowlist count pins and the human-only fence tests are unchanged and green.
Auto-release consumes the criterion-bound dossier from the prerequisite row: an arm proves a dossier with a criterion gap is NOT auto-released even under an R0 opt-in, asserting the gap code.

pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test, pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test and pnpm test (packages/core policy) all EXIT 0 with count lines quoted; the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors are re-censused if any command kind or payload shape changed.

implementationPlan.description: PHASE 1-2, no file writes. Confirm the three children have LANDED and re-measure the surface they composed, because this row asserts a composition it does not own. Read get_context.epicSiblings for task-a47301ee3aa64866ba109d4c0283526f (mapping + carried opt-ins), task-b8571cfe50614c1d89fee3a0a448de10 (Gate 2) and task-24b68b05c865436ead05cd5ea375ff6f (Gate 3), taking each row's verification, completionSummary and reviewSummary as the authority rather than re-measuring HEAD. Then grep the delivered symbols this row will consume, and record command + result in a row comment: `git grep -n 'evaluatePolicy' -- apps/daemon/src/preview/ apps/daemon/src/release/` must now return non-test hits in BOTH directories (it returned nothing at plan time, 2026-09-09); `git grep -n 'autoApprovalOptIns: \[\]' -- apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts` must return NO match; and the risk-class-to-tier mapping module must exist under apps/control-room/src/v2/goals/. If any of these is still absent the children have not delivered what this row composes: STOP and report blocked naming the specific symbol, do NOT reimplement it here and do NOT narrow the DoD.

Add the UNATTENDED WORLD as a NEW small fixtures module beside the existing one. HARD CONSTRAINT measured at plan time: apps/daemon/src/gates-journey-fixtures.ts is 387 lines against the 400 hard per-file cap, so do NOT grow it - create apps/daemon/src/gates-unattended-fixtures.ts and re-export or import from the existing fixtures rather than duplicating the world. The module builds a journey world whose installed policy slice CARRIES auto-approval opt-ins for both gate actions, parameterised by tier so one helper serves the R0/R1, R2/R3 and gap cases. Read the two action strings from the kind constants (PREVIEW_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND at preview/preview-contracts.ts:43 and RELEASE_DECIDE_COMMAND_KIND from release/release-decide-contracts.ts) - never hand-type the literals, which drift. Respect foldSlices semantics measured at policy-composition.ts:132-170: only the LAST slice's autoApprovalOptIns are in effect, so an opt-in placed on an earlier slice silently does nothing and would make every arm below vacuous. Keep this file under 250 lines.

DoD item 1 - the happy path. Add the UNATTENDED JOURNEY arm to apps/daemon/src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts: a goal whose risk class maps to R0 or R1, with an approved plan at Gate 1, reaches a DEPLOYED preview and then a released PR with ZERO further human decisions. Follow the file's binding house style stated in its header: read every end state back FROM THE STORE through a production reader (readPreviewDecision, readReleaseReceipt), never from the command's return value, because a DurableDecision carries no verdict and an arm on it proves only that the function returned. The arm must assert that EACH gate's persisted decision record NAMES the durable opt-in it acted under - assert the recorded action and tier field values, not merely that the outcome was APPROVE/ACCEPTED. An arm that only checks the verdict would pass identically against a human decision and would not test this row's subject.

DoD item 2 - the tier negative. Add the arm proving a goal mapped to R2 or R3 is NOT auto-approved at EITHER gate: each gate stays pending for a human, and the refusal carries the specific reason code HUMAN_ONLY_TIER together with the LAYER that answered, per the file's stated rule that ordering and refusal are proven by code plus layer and never by mere failure. Add the companion invariant arm asserting POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS imported from the @moe/core bare specifier still deep-equals ['R0','R1'], and that this row modified no file under packages/core/src/policy/ (assert via the imported constant, not a re-typed literal). This row does not widen the auto-approval tiers and the arm is what pins that.

DoD item 3 - human REJECT wins. Add the arm that records a MANUAL REJECT at a gate and then proves the automatic path does not overturn it, asserting the refusal's stable code AND the layer that refused. VACUITY IS THE REAL RISK HERE: this arm is one added refusal layer away from meaningless, because a second layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing precedence - so assert WHICH layer answered, and verify non-vacuity by mutating the precedence check in the delivered production module and confirming this arm goes RED. Drill safety, binding: `git status --porcelain` the exact path first; copy it out of tree to %TEMP% with a backup name carrying THIS task id (not only the worker id, which is reused across relaunches and has held stale vintages); restore by copying the backup back; prove the restore by SHA256 equality against the pre-mutation hash in a call SEPARATE from the restore. Never use `git checkout --` or `git restore` while other rows are mid-delivery on this shared tree.

DoD item 6 - the criterion-gap arm. Add the arm proving a release dossier carrying a CRITERION GAP is NOT auto-released even under a valid R0 opt-in, asserting the specific stable gap code and the layer that refused. This is the defect the 2026-09-09 external review found: auto-releasing on a dossier weaker than goal closure demands. Read the gap code from the vocabulary landed by task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada (the criterion-bound dossier row, which child C depends on) - grep the delivered constant and assert the imported symbol; never invent a code here, and never re-implement the dossier's gap detection inside the test, which would prove only that the test agrees with itself.

DoD items 5 (second half) and 7 - the fence census and the verification gate, concentrated here rather than smeared across the steps above. Prove no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision: run the existing human-only fence and roster coherence legs and confirm both gate kinds are still in OPERATOR_PRINCIPAL_KINDS and still in MCP_EXCLUDED_COMMAND_KINDS, asserted BOTH directions per global rail 9 - enumerate the served set from the dispatch seam, not only from the roster constant, since a test that iterates the roster alone shrinks with it and stays green. Per epic rail 3 do NOT freeze any count literal: run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative. Then run the three gates and quote each count line verbatim in the completion record: `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, and `pnpm test` for the packages/core policy arms. Read the OUTPUT, not the exit code - a `--filter` leg prints 'No projects matched the filters' and EXITS 0 for a name that is not a workspace package, and 'No test files found' is also exit 0, so the discriminator is the `Test Files N passed` line and the count must be NONZERO. Note that `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** tests, so the two per-package legs are the only evidence for the app packages. Finally re-census the four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors with a full-tree `git grep` of the literal across ALL file types; if the children changed no command kind or payload shape, state that explicitly and quote the census output rather than claiming it silently.

PHASE 7 - adversarial self-review before complete_task, reading the diff as an attacker rather than its author. Specifically: could any arm added here pass against a HUMAN decision as readily as an automatic one (if so it does not test this row's subject)? Does any arm assert only that an operation refused, without pinning the code and the layer? Is any arm's opt-in placed on a non-final slice, which foldSlices would silently drop and make the arm vacuous? Would a reviewer be able to distinguish an automatic approval from a human one by reading only the persisted record? Does anything here widen POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS, edit a roster constant, or touch the MCP allowlist - all forbidden by this row and by the 2026-09-06 governor ruling? Confirm the shared-tree discipline held: report every path created or modified in complete_step.modifiedFiles, and confirm none of the 28 pre-existing dirty paths belonging to other sessions were reverted, stashed or committed. Record the review outcome in the completion record; if it exceeds the 2000-char summary cap, put the load-bearing detail in a row comment FIRST, since completionSummary truncates silently mid-word.

comments.content:
SPIDR SPLIT 2026-09-09 by architect-fa84777a, with the owner in the REPL. This row is now the INTEGRATION row; three children carry the production bytes. dependsOn is set to all three (previousDependsOn was [task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada], now carried by child C instead).

WHY THE SPLIT. Measured at HEAD before planning, not taken from the description:
- `git grep -ln "evaluatePolicy|PolicyRiskTier|autoApprovalOptIns" -- apps/daemon/src/preview/** apps/daemon/src/release/**` returns NOTHING. Neither gate consults the policy engine at all. The description's framing ("the engine already exists and is dark") is true of the two seams it names but understates this: there is no policy call at either gate, so this row BUILDS a consumption path rather than lighting an existing one. Honest file count was ~20 across packages/core, apps/control-room and apps/daemon, against a 10-file hard reject.

CHILDREN, in build order:
- A task-a47301ee3aa64866ba109d4c0283526f - AdvisoryRiskClass -> PolicyRiskTier mapping + live dispatch carries opt-ins. NO dependencies; this is the leaf, plan it first.
- B task-b8571cfe50614c1d89fee3a0a448de10 - Gate 2 / preview.decide auto-decision. dependsOn [A].
- C task-24b68b05c865436ead05cd5ea375ff6f - Gate 3 / release.decide auto-decision. dependsOn [A, task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada].

B is deliberately ahead of C: Gate 2 waits on no unlanded evidence row, while C's dossier prerequisite task-b8ec9a638f6540c28798c29f23fd5ada is MEASURED at status PLANNING with commits 0. Gate 2 can go unattended without waiting for it.

DoD RE-SCOPING, recorded here because the field is not editable in place. The seven DoD items stand as written; what changes is WHO DISCHARGES EACH. This row does NOT re-implement child work - it asserts the composition:
- Items 1, 2, 3 and 6 (the journey arm, the R2/R3 negative, manual REJECT wins, the criterion-gap arm) are THIS ROW's, proven at the composed sequence in apps/daemon/src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts.
- Item 4 (the typed mapping, arms on totality) is discharged by child A. This row asserts only that the mapping composes into a live goal, and does not re-assert A's unit arms.
- Item 5 splits: "production no longer passes autoApprovalOptIns: [] unconditionally" is child A's; "no agent seat or MCP tool can submit a gate decision, allowlist and fence tests unchanged and green" is THIS ROW's census.
- Item 7 (three test legs + digest mirror census) is THIS ROW's.

OWNER RULING on DoD item 4's arithmetic. As written it asked for set equality both directions between 3 AdvisoryRiskClass values and 4 POLICY_RISK_TIERS, which no total function satisfies (a 3-set cannot surject onto a 4-set). The owner chose to drop the reachability half and keep totality and injectivity. The mapping is STANDARD->R0, ELEVATED->R1, RESTRICTED->R3, with R2 deliberately unreachable from the form. Nothing is weakened: policy-evaluation.ts:155-158 returns REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL with HUMAN_ONLY_TIER for R2 and R3 alike. POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS is NOT widened by any row in this split.

TWO create_task WARNINGS ARE FALSE POSITIVES HERE, recorded so a grader does not read them as ignored guidance. (1) The "meta/hardening row already exists" warning fired on children B and C by title heuristic; both ship production bytes (a policy consumption path at a gate), they are not evidence rows, so the fold-in instruction does not apply. This row remains the single integration row. (2) The "title contains and" warning on child A is correct English but wrong here: a mapping with no call site would be a pure module with no consumer edge, which the composition rail forbids, so the mapping and its one consumer must land together.

PLANNING CONSTRAINT for whoever executes this row: apps/daemon/src/gates-journey-fixtures.ts is at 387 lines against the 400 hard per-file cap. Add a NEW small fixtures module for the unattended world; do not grow that file.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: REJECTED - keeping this as one row. Measured ~20 files across packages/core, apps/control-room and apps/daemon against a 10-file hard reject; epic rail 1 already says a change of this shape is a four-row job. REJECTED - carrying provenance on the WIRE payload. decodePreviewDecidePayload enforces exact arity (APPROVE is exactly ['decision','previewRef'], any extra key refused with PREVIEW_DECISION_INVALID), so provenance there rotates all four GENERATED_CONTRACT_DIGEST mirrors. Measured instead that the PERSISTED record (PREVIEW_DECISION_VERSION/PREVIEW_DECISION_KEYS at preview-daemon-edge.ts:62-77) is pinned by nothing outside apps/daemon, so child B records provenance there and no mirror rotates. REJECTED - filing a separate 'unattended journey' evidence row. This row already IS the integration row at order 80 and create_task warns against a second one; the journey arm stays here. REJECTED - a new approval-policy subsystem. assessTier at policy-evaluation.ts:150-166 is the decision and must be CALLED, never reimplemented.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: MEASURED AT HEAD 2026-09-09, commands and results. (1) `git grep -ln 'evaluatePolicy|PolicyRiskTier|autoApprovalOptIns' -- apps/daemon/src/preview/** apps/daemon/src/release/**` returns NOTHING - neither gate consults the policy engine today; this is the fact that forced the split. (2) Engine confirmed present: policy-evaluation.ts:150-166 assessTier, R2/R3 -> REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL + HUMAN_ONLY_TIER (:155-158), no matching opt-in -> AUTO_APPROVAL_NOT_OPTED_IN (:165), match requires `entry.action === action && tierRank(entry.tier) >= tierRank(tier)`; policy-contract.ts:28 POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS = ['R0','R1']. (3) Seam one: `autoApprovalOptIns: []` at apps/control-room/src/live/live-dispatch-payloads.ts:100 is the ONLY production caller, every other hit is a fixture or test. (4) Seam two: AdvisoryRiskClass at goal-model.ts:90, set at new-goal-form.tsx:55/215, consumed only as prose in briefOfDraft in live-goal-create.ts. (5) TYPE-LEVEL FENCE: PolicyAutoApprovalOptIn.tier is PolicyAutoApprovalTier (R0|R1), so an opt-in CANNOT carry R2/R3 - the compiler refuses it. (6) foldSlices (policy-composition.ts:132-170) returns the LAST slice's optIns; an opt-in absent from the final slice is not in effect. (7) Dependency edge apps/control-room -> @moe/core VERIFIED all three ways: package.json declares 'workspace:*', pnpm-lock.yaml carries the apps/control-room importer at line 70, and production code already imports the bare specifier at approvals/approval-gating.ts:4. No manifest edit needed. Barrel exports POLICY_RISK_TIERS/POLICY_AUTO_APPROVAL_TIERS/PolicyRiskTier at policy-public.ts:40,45,63. (8) THE ANCHOR for this row: apps/daemon/src/gates-compose-journey.test.ts (168 lines) is the only place the four-decision operator SEQUENCE exists; its world lives in gates-journey-fixtures.ts (387 lines, against a 400 hard cap - do NOT grow it). Its house style is binding and matches this row's DoD: every end state is read back from the store through a production reader because a DurableDecision carries no verdict, and ordering is proven by REFUSAL asserting the specific code AND the layer that answered.
planningNotes.risks: ORDERING: this row is gated by dependsOn on all three children and must not be executed before they are DONE - read their verification and completionSummary from get_context.epicSiblings rather than re-measuring HEAD. PER-FILE CAP: gates-journey-fixtures.ts is at 387/400 lines; adding the unattended world to it breaches the cap, so add a new small module. ROSTER COUNTS: epic rail 3 forbids freezing a count literal in a gate - run the leg and take the PRINTED expected-vs-received as authoritative, because a concurrent kind-publishing row moves those literals. VACUITY: a manual-REJECT-wins arm is one added refusal layer away from vacuous - a second layer can answer first and the arm stays green while no longer testing precedence, so assert WHICH layer refused and verify by mutation. APPS/** COVERAGE: `pnpm test` runs ZERO tests under apps/**, so repo-wide green claims here are false unless the two per-package legs are run and quoted. SHARED TREE: 28 dirty paths belong to other sessions; never revert, stash or commit foreign paths.
